items.title: PyTorch 2.15.0 Release
items.abstract_or_text: # PyTorch 2.15.0 Release Notes - [Highlights](#highlights) - [Backwards Incompatible Changes](#backwards-incompatible-changes) - [Deprecations](#deprecations) - [New Features](#new-features) - [Improvements](#improvements) - [Bug fixes](#bug-fixes) - [Performance](#performance) - [Documentation](#documentation) - [Security](#security) - [Developers](#developers) # Highlights Rewritten NCCL backend becomes the default , with a flight recorder that dumps on hangs and TORCH_DIST_USE_NCCL2=0 or nccl-legacy as rollback paths One-sided transports for torch.distributed , with a NIXL backend and CUDA-graph-capturable transfers FSDP2 and pipelining gain finer memory and communication control , with fp32 for precision-sensitive parameters, CUDA-graph-captured gradient accumulation, and gradient reduction overlapped with compute Faster 4-bit (NVFP4) LLM decoding on NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs through fewer, better-overlapped kernel launches in NVGEMM Apple Silicon gains FP8 and faster decode , with float8_e4m3fn and _scaled_mm , a new grouped_mm with a decode fast path (1.32–1.34x tokens/s on MoE decode), and public torch.mps.Stream APIs Broader platform support with FlyDSL kernels on AMD gfx950, Tensor Data Mover support for gfx1250 (MI450), ROCm 10.0 wheels, simpler SYCL kernel authoring and multi-GPU profiling on Intel GPUs, CUDA 13.2 as the default wheel with CUDA 13.4 alongside it, and torch.compile on Python 3.15 For more details about these highlighted features, you can look at the release blogpost. Below are the full release notes for this release. # Backwards Incompatible Changes ## Python Frontend ### `import torch` can no longer be re-executed in the same process, including via `importlib.reload(torch)` (#194654) `importlib.reload(torch)` and `del sys.modules["torch"]` + re-import now raise, as does retrying `import torch` after it failed. Re-running the module body was already unsafe in exactly the same way as the retry, so the new check does not distinguish the two. Normal use is unaffected: a successful import leaves `torch` in `sys.modules` so the body never re-runs, and re-entrant imports from a backend extension during autoload still short-circuit on `sys.modules` without reaching the check. Version 2.14: ```python import importlib import torch importlib.reload(torch) # RuntimeError: Only a single TORCH_LIBRARY can be used to register the namespace triton; ... # (re-importing after a failed `import torch` failed with similarly misleading errors or could segfault) ``` Version 2.15: ```python import importlib import torch importlib.reload(torch) # ImportError: `torch` can only be initialized once per process, so this module cannot # be imported again: neither via `importlib.reload(torch)`, nor by re-importing after # a failed `import torch`. ``` ### Nested tensors are no longer allowlisted for `torch.load(..., weights_only=True)` (#194380) Nested jagged and strided nested tensors are no longer on the default `weights_only` allowlist. Loading a checkpoint that contains one with `weights_only=True` (the default) now fails with `Unsupported global: GLOBAL torch.nested._internal.nested_tensor._rebuild_njt was not an allowed global by default` (or `GLOBAL torch._utils._rebuild_nested_tensor` for strided nested tensors). To load checkpoints containing nested tensors, allow them explicitly with `torch.serialization.safe_globals` (see below), or use `weights_only=False` for trusted files. Version 2.14: ```python loaded = torch.load("njt.pt", weights_only=True) # works ``` Version 2.15: ```python from torch.nested._internal.nested_tensor import _rebuild_njt, NestedTensor with torch.serialization.safe_globals([_rebuild_njt, NestedTensor]): loaded = torch.load("njt.pt", weights_only=True) ``` ### Operators called through `torch.ops.*` and `torch._C._dispatch_call_boxed` now use PyTorch's own warning and exception translation instead of pybind11's (#193451) We make `torch.ops.*` calls go through the same exception and warning translation as the rest of the library. This means that some exception translation that used to be handled by pybind is now handled natively. User-defined pybind exception translation is thus lost. Restoring it may be done in a future release as part of a broader exception handler improvement. In addition, `TORCH_WARN` warnings from these operators now reach Python's `warnings` module, so they raise when warnings are turned into errors (`-W error`). `std::out_of_range` still becomes `IndexError` (#195713). Version 2.14: ```python # C++ op: throw std::invalid_argument("bad size"); try: torch.ops.my_lib.my_op(x) except ValueError: # pybind11 translation ... ``` Version 2.15: ```python # C++ op: TORCH_CHECK_VALUE(false, "bad size"); try: torch.ops.my_lib.my_op(x) except ValueError: ... # TORCH_WARN from the op is now a Python warning with warnings.catch_warnings(): warnings.simplefilter("ignore") torch.ops.my_lib.my_op(x) ``` ## Autograd ### Selective activation checkpointing now saves, rather than recomputes, the outputs of operators with an ordered effect unless the policy returns `CheckpointPolicy.MUST_RECOMPUTE` (#196956) In eager mode, if a `create_selective_checkpoint_contexts` policy returns `CheckpointPolicy.PREFER_RECOMPUTE` for a non-aliasing operator with an ordered effect (e.g. via `register_effect(torch.library.EffectType.ORDERED)`), that choice is now overridden and its outputs are saved, so the side effect is no longer replayed during backward. This can increase activation memory. To keep the 2.14 behavior, return `CheckpointPolicy.MUST_RECOMPUTE` for that operator. Operators in the `c10d` namespace are excluded. Under `torch.compile`, `CheckpointPolicy.MUST_RECOMPUTE` on an effectful operator now raises at compile time: `RuntimeError: AOTAutograd does not support MUST_RECOMPUTE for effectful operations because forward effects cannot join the backward effect-token chain.` Use a save policy instead. ```python policy = lambda ctx, op, *args, **kwargs: CheckpointPolicy.PREFER_RECOMPUTE checkpoint(fn, x, use_reentrant=False, context_fn=lambda: create_selective_checkpoint_contexts(policy)) # 2.14: an effectful op in fn runs twice; 2.15: once (use CheckpointPolicy.MUST_RECOMPUTE to replay) ``` ## Distributed (c10d) ### The `nccl` backend now uses a rewritten, cleaned-up NCCL implementation by default (#192281, #192895, #193237, #193241) `backend="nccl"` (also the default CUDA backend of `init_process_group()`) now creates the new implementation. The legacy implementation is available as `backend="nccl-legacy"` for this release only: **`nccl-legacy` and `TORCH_DIST_USE_NCCL2=0` will be removed in the next release**, so migrate to `nccl` or `nccl-lazy`. Use `nccl` (eager initialization) by default. Use `nccl-lazy` when you need independent point-to-point communicators: collectives run on one eagerly created communicator, and each send/recv peer pair gets its own lazily created communicator and stream, so concurrent P2P to different peers can overlap (as in the legacy backend). Differences from the legacy backend: - Communicators are created eagerly in `init_process_group()`/`new_group()`, allocating GPU memory even for unused groups. - Each group is bound to one CUDA device: `device_id`, else `LOCAL_RANK % torch.cuda.device_count()` (or the global rank modulo the device count); `torch.cuda.set_device()` is not used. Tensors on another GPU fail with `Expected tensor on cuda:X but found tensor on cuda:Y` or `ProcessGroupNCCL is bound to device cuda:X but an operation was issued on cuda:Y`. Pass `device_id` if needed; several GPUs per process requires `nccl-legacy`. - `dist.get_backend_impl(...)` returns the new backend class, so `isinstance(..., ProcessGroupNCCL)` is `False` and legacy-only methods such as `comm_split_count()` are missing. - An async `all_gather`'s `work.get_future()` value is the list of per-rank outputs, not a one-element list holding a stacked tensor; read the output list passed to `all_gather` instead (works on both backends). To temporarily restore the legacy behavior in 2.15, set `TORCH_DIST_USE_NCCL2=0` on every rank before creating the process group, or use `nccl-legacy`: Version 2.14: ```python dist.init_process_group("nccl") # ProcessGroupNCCL ``` Version 2.15: ```python dist.init_process_group("nccl", device_id=torch.device("cuda", local_rank)) # new implementation dist.init_process_group("nccl-lazy", device_id=torch.device("cuda", local_rank)) # independent P2P communicators dist.init_process_group("nccl-legacy") # legacy implementation, removed in the next release ``` ## Distributed Checkpointing ### Distributed checkpoint metadata now records tensor strides, so checkpoints saved with PyTorch 2.15 cannot be loaded by PyTorch 2.14 or earlier (#194251) `TensorProperties` gains an optional `strides` field in the pickled `.metadata` file. In older versions `dcp.load` raises a `CheckpointException` reporting `too many values to unpack (expected 5)`. There is no flag to write the old format. Version 2.14 (loading a 2.15 checkpoint): ```python dcp.load(state_dict, checkpoint_id="/ckpt/step_100") # CheckpointException: ... too many values to unpack (expected 5) ``` Version 2.15: ```python dcp.load(state_dict, checkpoint_id="/ckpt/step_100") # loads 2.14 and 2.15 checkpoints ``` ## Distributed FSDP2 ### With `MixedPrecisionPolicy(reduce_dtype=None)`, `fully_shard` now accumulates and reduces gradients in the parameter's `grad_dtype` (its original dtype by default) instead of in `param_dtype` (#194434) **This is BC-breaking**: `mp_policy.reduce_dtype=None` no longer defaults to `mp_policy.param_dtype`. * [popular case] fp32 params, `MixedPrecisionPolicy(param_dtype=bf16)` * before: grad accumulation and reduce happen in bf16 * after: grad accumulation and reduce happen in fp32 (2x reduce-scatter bytes) * [rare case] bf16 params, `MixedPrecisionPolicy(param_dtype=fp32)` * before: grad accumulation and reduce happen in fp32 * after: grad accumulation and reduce happen in bf16 How to deal with BC: explicitly set `mp_policy.reduce_dtype`. In grad accumulation (no reduce-scatter), the unsharded param's `.grad` always holds the accumulated value, visible via `model.parameters()` while unsharded. Before this change, `.grad` was `None` when `reduce_dtype` was set and differed from `param_dtype` (FSDP kept the sum in a hidden `reduce_dtype` buffer). Version 2.14: ```python # fp32 parameters mp_policy = MixedPrecisionPolicy(param_dtype=torch.bfloat16) fully_shard(model, mp_policy=mp_policy) # gradients accumulate and reduce-scatter in bf16 ``` Version 2.15: ```python # fp32 parameters mp_policy = MixedPrecisionPolicy(param_dtype=torch.bfloat16) fully_shard(model, mp_policy=mp_policy) # gradients accumulate and reduce-scatter in fp32 # to keep the 2.14 behavior, set reduce_dtype explicitly mp_policy = MixedPrecisionPolicy(param_dtype=torch.bfloat16, reduce_dtype=torch.bfloat16) fully_shard(model, mp_policy=mp_policy) ``` ## Distributed Pipelining ### `torch.distributed.config.pipeline_per_direction_p2p` is renamed to `pipeline_per_edge_p2p` and now uses one communicator per directed rank-to-rank edge (#196666) The old names were removed with no alias: setting the attribute raises `AttributeError: torch.distributed.config.pipeline_per_direction_p2p does not exist`, and `TORCH_DISTRIBUTED_PIPELINE_PER_DIRECTION_P2P` is silently ignored. Version 2.14: ```python dist_config.pipeline_per_direction_p2p = True ``` Version 2.15: ```python dist_config.pipeline_per_edge_p2p = True # or TORCH_DISTRIBUTED_PIPELINE_PER_EDGE_P2P=1 ``` ## Profiler ### C++ stack traces are now symbolized with `dladdr` instead of `addr2line` by default (#195462) `TORCH_DISABLE_ADDR2LINE` now defaults to on, since `addr2line` is slow and can hang. C++ frames in `TORCH_SHOW_CPP_STACKTRACES=1` errors and CUDA memory snapshots now show the library path and offset, plus the symbol name only if exported (otherwise `??`). To restore `addr2line`, set `TORCH_DISABLE_ADDR2LINE=0` or `TORCH_SYMBOLIZE_MODE=addr2line`. ```bash TORCH_SHOW_CPP_STACKTRACES=1 TORCH_DISABLE_ADDR2LINE=0 python train.py ``` ### CUDA memory snapshots record the allocator's `mallocWithAddress` tag in a new `internal_metadata` field instead of appending it to `user_metadata` (#193432) `user_metadata` in `torch.cuda.memory._snapshot()` trace entries is now exactly what was set with `torch.cuda.memory._set_memory_metadata` (which now also accepts a dict). Tools that searched `user_metadata` for `mallocWithAddress` must read `internal_metadata` instead. ```python # 2.14 tagged = [e for e in trace if "mallocWithAddress" in e["user_metadata"]] # 2.15 tagged = [e for e in trace if e.get("internal_metadata") == "mallocWithAddress"] ``` ### Remove the deprecated `FunctionEvent.metadata_json` property (#198265) Accessing it now raises `AttributeError: 'FunctionEvent' object has no attribute 'metadata_json'`, and the `metadata_json` constructor argument is removed. Use `FunctionEvent.metadata`, a dict populated when `_ExperimentalConfig(expose_kineto_event_metadata=True)` is set (not the deprecated `event_metadata`). ```python metadata = event.metadata_json # 2.14: JSON string metadata = event.metadata # 2.15: dict[str, Any] or None ``` ### Rename the experimental CUPTI monitor profiler backend to Cuspy, without aliases for the old names (#195881) In `_ExperimentalConfig(custom_profiler_config=...)`, `"cupti_monitor"` is now `"cuspy"` and `"cupti_monitor_async_export"` is now `"cuspy_async_export"`; old names silently fall back to the default Kineto backend. `prof.take_pending_cupti_export()` is now `take_pending_cuspy_export()` (the old name raises `AttributeError`). Prefer the new `torch.profiler.CuspyConfig`. ```python # 2.14 cfg = _ExperimentalConfig(custom_profiler_config='{"backend":"cupti_monitor"}') # 2.15 cfg = _ExperimentalConfig(custom_profiler_config='{"backend":"cuspy"}') ``` ## Dynamo ### Higher-order ops now reject input mutation and aliasing in their bodies unless the op opts in (#185738) Before, Dynamo let any higher-order op body mutate or alias its inputs by default. Ops that do not implement those semantics could silently produce invalid graphs. Mutation and aliasing are now off by default. The built-in wrappers that support them (`wrap`, checkpoint, `autograd.Function`, autocast/set-grad wrappers) opt in. A `flex_attention` `mask_mod` may read captured views but must not mutate inputs or return aliases. Under `fullgraph=True`, unsupported mutation or aliasing raises `Encountered input mutation during higher order op tracing` or `Encountered aliasing during higher order op tracing`; otherwise, Dynamo graph breaks and falls back to eager execution. Rewrite the higher-order op body to avoid mutation or aliasing. For example, rewrite an in-place `flex_attention` score modifier as an out-of-place operation: Version 2.14: ```python def score_mod(score, b, h, q, k): score.add_(1) return score.clone() ``` Version 2.15: ```python def score_mod(score, b, h, q, k): return score + 1 ``` ## Inductor ### `torch.compiler.nested_compile_region(options=...)` now accepts only an allowlist of Inductor config patches (#195864, #195865) Patches passed through `get_invoke_subgraph_compile_options(fw_inductor_config_patches=..., bw_inductor_config_patches=...)` used to accept any `torch._inductor.config` key, though many were silently ignored. Only `fallback_by_default` and `max_autotune` are now accepted; other keys raise `ValueError: Inductor config key ' ' is not supported in forward nested compile-region options` (or `backward`). Apply other options to the whole compiled function. Patch dictionaries are now snapshotted when the options are created, so later mutation has no effect, and the default no longer implicitly sets `triton.autotune_at_compile_time=True`. Version 2.14: ```python opts = get_invoke_subgraph_compile_options(fw_inductor_config_patches={"triton.multi_kernel": 1}) ``` Version 2.15: ```python opts = get_invoke_subgraph_compile_options(fw_inductor_config_patches={"max_autotune": True}) compiled = torch.compile(fn, options={"triton.multi_kernel": 1}) ``` ### `torch.compiler.precompile` is now a module instead of a callable; capture with `torch.compiler.precompile.capture(...)` and reload with `torch.compiler.precompile.load(...)` (#197993, #198135, #198213) Calling `torch.compiler.precompile(fn, *example_inputs)` now raises `TypeError: 'module' object is not callable`. `capture(fn, *, artifact_path, cache_path)` returns a context manager that you call once inside the `with` block; it writes both files when the block exits cleanly (or on `cap.save()`), and `load` now takes those paths. `decompositions=` moves to `tracer=MakeFxTracer(decompositions=...)`. Version 2.14: ```python python_code, cache = torch.compiler.precompile(lambda m, x: m(x), model, x) f = torch.compiler.precompile.load(python_code, cache) ``` Version 2.15: ```python with torch.compiler.precompile.capture(lambda m, x: m(x), artifact_path="m.py", cache_path="m.cache") as cap: cap(model, x) f = torch.compiler.precompile.load("m.py", "m.cache") ``` ## Composability ### Under functionalization, a regenerated output of `split`, `split_with_sizes` or `unbind` is now rebuilt as a single `slice` or `select` of its base, so its `grad_fn` is `SliceBackward0`/`SelectBackward0` instead of `SplitBackward0`/`SplitWithSizesBackward0`/`UnbindBackward0` (#194037) This greatly reduces compile time for code that mutates many `split()` views (for example 32s to 15s with 128 views). Gradients are unchanged, but the in-place error now names the new op with output index 0: `RuntimeError: Output 0 of Select is a view and is being modified inplace.` Code that inspects `grad_fn` names, matches the old error text, or pattern-matches `split`/`unbind` nodes in functionalized graphs needs updating. There is no option to restore the previous behavior. Version 2.14: ```python >>> out = torch.func.functionalize(f)(x) # f returns base.unbind(0)[1] after base.add_(1) >>> out.grad_fn ``` Version 2.15: ```python >>> out = torch.func.functionalize(f)(x) >>> out.grad_fn ``` ## Release Engineering ### PyPI wheels now ship with CUDA 13.2, and CUDA 12.6 and CUDA 13.0 wheels are no longer published (#196249, #198913) The default PyPI wheel moves from CUDA 13.0 to CUDA 13.2. The 2.15 wheels are `cu132` and `cu134`; `cu126` and `cu130` are no longer built. CUDA 13 wheels need NVIDIA driver 580 or newer and a GPU of Turing (`sm_75`) or newer, so Maxwell, Pascal and Volta GPUs and hosts with a CUDA 12.x driver should stay on 2.14. Version 2.15: ```bash # PyPI wheel now uses CUDA 13.2 pip install torch # CUDA 13.4 wheels pip install torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu134 # To stay on CUDA 12.6 or CUDA 13.0, pin PyTorch 2.14: pip install torch==2.14.0 --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu126 # or cu130 ``` ### Python 3.10 wheels are no longer published (#198233, #199398) PyTorch 2.15 raises the minimum supported Python version for binaries to 3.11: no `cp310` wheels are built for `torch` or the Triton wheels, and CI no longer tests on Python 3.10. On Python 3.10, `pip` cannot find a 2.15 wheel. Upgrade to Python 3.11 or newer, or stay on PyTorch 2.14. Version 2.14: ```bash python3.10 -m pip install torch # cp310 wheel available ``` Version 2.15: ```bash python3.11 -m pip install torch==2.15.0 # Python 3.11 through 3.15 (including 3.14t and 3.15t) ``` ### ROCm wheels move to ROCm 7.14 and 10.0; ROCm 7.2 wheels and gfx900/gfx906 kernels are dropped (#194919) gfx900 (MI25) and gfx906 (MI50/MI60, Radeon VII) users can stay on 2.14 (`rocm7.2`) or build from source with those targets in `PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH`. ```bash pip install torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/rocm7.14 # or rocm10.0 ``` ### Linux CUDA wheels no longer depend on the cuRAND library (#194850) PyTorch only uses the cuRAND device API, so `torch` no longer links `libcurand`, no longer preloads it on `import torch`, and the wheel's CUDA requirements no longer include cuRAND. Extensions or libraries that call the cuRAND host API (for example `curandCreateGenerator`) and relied on `pip install torch` bringing in the cuRAND library can fail to load `libcurand.so` and must now install it themselves. Version 2.15: ```bash pip install torch pip install "cuda-toolkit[curand]==13.2.2" # match the toolkit version of your wheel ``` ## CUDA ### `torch.histc(..., out=...)` on CUDA now raises an error when `out` does not have the same dtype as the input (#196100) CUDA used to silently cast into any `out` dtype. It now matches CPU and MPS and rejects mismatches, even widening ones. Compute without `out` and cast instead. Version 2.14: ```python >>> torch.histc(x, bins=4, min=-2.0, max=2.0, out=int64_out) # silently truncated ``` Version 2.15: ```python RuntimeError: torch.histogram: input tensor and hist tensor should have the same dtype, but got input float and hist long int >>> int64_out.copy_(torch.histc(x, bins=4, min=-2.0, max=2.0)) # workaround ``` ### On CUDA, cuBLAS and cuBLASLt workspaces are now allocated for each operation instead of being cached per handle and stream (#194311) Graphs captured separately on one stream could share the cached workspace and fail on replay with `CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered`. Workspaces are now freed after each op, so `torch.cuda.memory_allocated()` excludes them and the handle from `torch.cuda.current_blas_handle()` has no ATen workspace attached. Set `TORCH_CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CACHE=1` to restore caching (unsafe with multiple graphs on one stream). `TORCH_CUBLASLT_UNIFIED_WORKSPACE` now only takes effect with caching enabled. ROCm has a matching change (#196920). Version 2.14: ```python >>> torch.mm(a, a, out=out) >>> torch.cuda.memory_allocated() - before > 0 # workspace stays allocated True ``` Version 2.15: ```python >>> torch.cuda.memory_allocated() - before # freed after the op 0 ``` ## CPU (AArch64) ### Float32 `torch.sin` and `torch.cos` on Arm CPUs (NEON and SVE) now use SLEEF's 3.5-ULP kernels instead of the 1.0-ULP kernels, matching the accuracy of the x86 AVX2 implementation and running 1.7x-2.4x faster on Neoverse V1/V2 (#196315) Float32 `sin` and `cos` results on Arm can now differ from earlier releases in the last bits. Bit-for-bit comparisons against stored golden outputs, `torch.equal`, or `torch.testing.assert_close` with `rtol=0, atol=0` may fail; default `assert_close` tolerances are unaffected. There is no switch to restore the previous kernels; if you need tighter accuracy, compute in float64 and cast back. Version 2.14: ```python >>> x.cos() # float32 on Arm: within 1 ULP ``` Version 2.15: ```python >>> x.cos() # float32 on Arm: within 2 ULP >>> x.double().cos().float() # workaround: correctly rounded ``` ## MPS ### The MPS backend now requires macOS 15 (Sequoia) or newer (#199261, #200290) macOS 14 has reached end of life, so its MPS workarounds were removed. On macOS 14, `torch.backends.mps.is_available()` returns `False` and allocating on `mps` raises the error below. To keep using MPS, stay on PyTorch 2.14 or upgrade macOS; CPU builds still run on older macOS. C++ extensions: `at::mps::MacOSVersion::MACOS_14_4` was removed. ```python >>> torch.ones(2, device="mps") # 2.15 on macOS 14 RuntimeError: The MPS backend is supported on macOS 15.0+. Current OS version can be queried using `sw_vers` ``` ## XPU ### Remove the `allocator` property from `torch.xpu.MemPool`, aligning with other accelerators (#192041) `torch.xpu.MemPool` no longer exposes the allocator it was constructed with, so `pool.allocator` now raises `AttributeError`. Keep your own reference to the allocator instead; passing one to the `MemPool` constructor is unchanged. Before: ```python pool = torch.xpu.MemPool(allocator.allocator()) my_allocator = pool.allocator ``` After: ```python my_allocator = allocator.allocator() pool = torch.xpu.MemPool(my_allocator) ``` ## Complex Frontend ### Ops that are undefined for complex inputs now raise `TypeError` instead of `RuntimeError` (#192350) This covers order-dependent ops (`sort`, `argsort`, `topk`, `argmax`/`argmin`, `max`/`min` with `dim`, `maximum`/`minimum`, `fmax`/`fmin`, `aminmax`), `isposinf`/`isneginf`, `view_as_real`/`imag` on real tensors, and `view_as_complex` on complex tensors, matching Python (`1j = 13.3) (#198419) ## cuDNN - Support causal grouped-query attention with a paged KV cache in the cuDNN backend of `torch.nn.attention.varlen` (`varlen_attn` and `varlen_attn_out`), enabling head dimension 256 with a paged KV cache on Blackwell GPUs; requires cuDNN 9.24 or newer (#195650) ## MPS - Add a public MPS stream API (`torch.mps.Stream`, `current_stream()`, `default_stream()`, `set_stream()`, the `torch.mps.stream()` context manager) and `Tensor.record_stream` on MPS (#191415, #193464) - Add `torch.float8_e4m3fn` support on MPS (#194074, #196915, #196918, #196945, #196955, #197383, #197801) - Support `float8_e4m3fn` inputs in `torch.nn.functional.scaled_mm` on MPS (#196916) ## XPU - SYCL Kernel Programming Simplified: Add SYCL free-function kernel support to the XPU backend and migrate most existing SYCL kernels to it, so device code can be written as explicit free functions in a more intuitive style instead of verbose functors (#196387, #196932, #198200, #198720, #200289) - Enhanced XPU Runtime Capabilities: Support sharing `torch.xpu.Event` across processes, through `torch.multiprocessing` or `ipc_handle()` / `from_ipc_handle()` on an event created with `interprocess=True` (#191182, #192495, #193399, #192514) - Improved XPU Profiling Experience: Add kernel-level visibility into XPU Graph replay, cross-rank correlation for XCCL collectives, and per-kernel hardware counter collection across all Intel GPUs in multi-GPU workloads to the XPU profiler (#195128, #198200) # Improvements ## Python Frontend - Saturate out-of-range integer scalar bounds in `clamp` and `hardtanh` instead of wrapping or raising (e.g. `torch.clamp(uint8_tensor, min=-255)` is a no-op) (#193169) - Support empty batch dimensions in FFT operations on CPU, CUDA and MPS (#190483) - Add `skip_unsupported` to `FlopCounterMode` to warn instead of failing on higher-order operators without a FLOP formula, and count `flex_attention` FLOPs (#167224) - Support `Optional[list[Tensor]]` annotations in `torch.library.infer_schema` and `custom_op` (#187012) - Make `torch.iinfo` and `torch.finfo` hashable (#193290) - Name the context manager in tracebacks through `torch.no_grad`-style decorators (#186502) - Improve type stubs for `Tensor @ scalar` and `torch.utils` re-exports (#195220, #195289) - Add `uint16`, `uint32` and `uint64` support to `torch.clamp`, `torch.maximum` and `torch.minimum` on CPU and CUDA (#189953) ## torch.nn - Support soft-label targets with `reduction="none"` on the chunked `linear_cross_entropy` path (#188296) - Allow FlashAttention-4 in `scaled_dot_product_attention` with different query/key and value head dimensions (#193039) - Support deterministic `bicubic` `F.interpolate` backward (#193707) - Support `bicubic` mode for 5-D input in `F.grid_sample` (#194787) - Allow `varlen_attn` to dispatch causal attention to cuDNN (#193630) - Add `weight` to the `F.mse_loss` type stub (#196126) ## Optimizer - Validate `lambd` and `alpha` in `torch.optim.ASGD` (#193303) - Reduce compile time: defer gen-2 GC while compiling (4.2s on one model; see `gc_gen2_threshold_during_compile`), skip empty graphs (custom backends are no longer called for such graphs), and speed up large functions (#193289, #193157, #195622) ## Inductor - Reduce compile time by caching in fusion search and codegen, hashing sources in the background, and compiling combo-kernel benchmarks in parallel (#186319, #192817, #192820, #194010, #194011, #198747, #198881, #198320) - Allow mix-order reduction fusion for more shapes, speeding up RMSNorm backward (#186370, #188660) - Reduce `cpp_wrapper` kernel call overhead by 40-50% (#192287) - Improve CPU FlexAttention BF16 performance by 6-29% (#191780) - Use larger reduction tiles on GB300, roughly doubling HBM bandwidth use (#193774) - Add gfx950 FlexAttention backward configs (1.8-2.3x faster) (#194151) - Improve NVGEMM NVFP4 decode performance on Blackwell and widen its autotuning candidates (#194651, #194652, #197485, #195539, #198293) - Compute only one triangle for large BF16 `X @ X.T` on SM100 (#194177, #194178) - Speed up collective bucketing, including up to 9x faster uneven reduce-scatter padding (#196647, #196621, #195616) - Simplify `slice_scatter` chains to reduce recomputation and peak memory (#192136, #195608, #195631) - Fix CPU OpenMP parallelization moving onto inner reduction loops under freezing, and recover an XPU inner-reduction regression (#190928, #190986) - Fuse `torch.cat`/`torch.stack` copies into foreach kernels for dynamic shapes (#198294) - Enable nested reduction fusion by default (`TORCHINDUCTOR_NESTED_REDUCTION=0` disables it), fusing patterns such as RMSNorm followed by MXFP8/NVFP4 quantization into one kernel (#190594, #190595, #191974, #193598, #196332, #196333, #196334) ## Ahead-Of-Time Inductor (AOTI) - Parallelize pinned host staging copies when loading CUDA constants (#195257) ## AOTDispatcher - Speed up the min-cut partitioner, reducing cold compile time by about 5% (#197724) ## Composability - Speed up FakeTensor view cache hits (#192821) - Reduce compile time in `ShapeEnv` (#193219, #193161, #195623) ## Quantization - Speed up AArch64 small-batch QNNPACK linear 2-4x (#193595) ## Foreach - Reduce `_foreach_norm`/`max` CUDA scratch memory (#190549) ## CUDA - Avoid CPU-GPU synchronization when assigning scalars through indexing on CUDA, e.g. `x[mask] = 1.0` (#189303, #188330, #198811) - Speed up CUDA `upsample_linear1d` by 5-25x for small outputs (#180885), pooling backward (#191086, #195119, #196156), dtype-conversion copies (#195542, #198723), 2D transpose copies (#194310), and `zero_` (#195303, #198565) - `torch.topk` on CUDA 13 Linux wheels uses ahead-of-time compiled radix-select kernels on Hopper and Blackwell (median 2.16x on H100) (#190899) - Fix a 10-30x slowdown of `gather`, `index_select`, `x[idx]` and `scatter_add` on rows of 16 or 32 bytes (#200995) ## cuDNN - Prefer the cuDNN backend for SDPA on sm86/sm89 for higher performance (#192799) ## CPU (x86) - Fix the CPU kernel dispatch cache never being populated, which made every dispatch to a CPU kernel repeat the CPU capability selection (#195328) ## CPU (AArch64) - Optimize `libtorch` code layout with LLVM BOLT, using profiles shipped in the repository. The new `USE_LLVM_BOLT` build option is on by default for Linux aarch64 CUDA builds when `llvm-bolt` 21 or newer is found and `USE_PRIORITIZED_TEXT_FOR_LD` is enabled, giving up to 30% faster workloads in some cases and up to 3% slower in others; set `USE_LLVM_BOLT=0` to opt out in source builds (#186245) - Use the native GEMV path for single-column (`n == 1`) BF16 GEMMs on Arm Neoverse CPUs built with oneDNN ACL, for about 5x faster single-thread GPT-2 BF16 decode on Graviton 4 and 5 (1.4x-2.7x with 8-64 threads on Graviton 5) (#198411) - Dispatch non-contiguous FP16 matmuls to oneDNN ACL GEMM kernels instead of the reference implementation on AArch64 (#198498) ## MPS - Move more MPS ops (`softmax`, `nll_loss`, padding, `where`, ...) to native Metal kernels, cutting launch overhead and driver memory growth with variable shapes (#196071, #195441, #195153, #195368, #193826, #198719, #198688, #198497, #196924, #189548, #199687, #198878) - Speed up MPS reductions, linear algebra, GEMV, convolutions, `histc`, masked fill, dropout and sort (#198494, #198611, #198635, #197397, #198646, #199278, #198721, #197862, #196241, #196900, #195944, #198732, #195950, #193623, #193167, #192164, #196016, #195020, #195011, #198960, #196922) - Speed up `softmax` over a non-innermost dim and `relu`, `clamp_min`, `leaky_relu` and other scalar-argument unary ops on row-strided views (#199758, #199933) ## XPU - Speed up SDPA training on XPU by aligning the oneDNN graph SDPA pattern with oneDNN v3.13 and integrating its GQA and dropout support (#195419) - Fuse the `GroupNorm` forward into a single kernel and speed up contiguous `cat` with vectorized stores on XPU (#194842) - Avoid register spilling in mixed fp32/bf16/fp16 elementwise kernels on XPU by adding vectorized type-casting loads (#194185) - Speed up `col2im` on XPU by replacing its hard-coded work-group size (#198720) - Reduce oneMKL LAPACK overhead on XPU by trimming scratchpad initialization, host synchronizations and re-allocation (#193110) ## JIT - Speed up `torch.jit.load` and graph pre-optimization (#194035, #193107, #193250, #194009) # Documentation ## Python Frontend - Document undefined behavior of bool tensors holding bytes other than 0/1, and clarify `Tensor.index_add_`'s `index` argument (#199012, #193403) ## torch.nn - Fix the `linear_cross_entropy` docstring snippet and `nn.RNN` example, and document bias with probability targets (#198941, #188433, #173888) ## Autograd - Document that custom `Function`/op backward gradients may have arbitrary strides and that `unpack_hook` order is unspecified (#195210, #198016) - Point `torch.utils.checkpoint` docs to `torch_remat` and drop the stale `use_reentrant` "version 2.9" error notice (#193998, #193720) - Fix math rendering on the autograd mechanics page (#192562) ## Distributed - Document the remaining NVSHMEM bindings (#193449) ## Distributed (c10d) - Add a tutorial for the distributed debug server (#178800) - Document `Backend.Options` and fix `irecv` and NCCL env var docs (#196123, #189623, #194701) ## Distributed FSDP2 - Document parameter-mutation limits of `fully_shard` (#198826) ## TorchElastic - Fix the `EtcdServer` example and `Worker` docstring (#198238, #199255) ## Profiler - Fix the `toggle_collection_dynamic` example (#190369) ## Dynamo - Remove references to the obsolete `dynamic_shapes` config (#198707) - Fix the PGO config example in the dynamic shapes docs (#191027) - Document more `torch._logging.set_logs` options (#188138) ## Inductor - Document the FlexAttention `ROWS_GUARANTEED_SAFE` requirement (#194154) ## Foreach - Fix in-place foreach type stubs to return the input list (#193466) ## Release Engineering - Fix docs search ranking module stub pages above the API symbols they document and listing duplicate results (#195042) - Link the build environment variable reference from `README.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md`, and fix outdated build instructions there (#193617) - Document the issue and pull request workflow in `CONTRIBUTING.md` and add a maintainer guide to the community docs (#198527) ## MPS - Note MPS lacks `float64` support (#193545) ## ROCm - Document gfx1151 SDPA layouts, hipFile GPUDirect Storage, and MI300 matmul precision issues (#190771, #195478, #190736) # Security ## Python Frontend - Fix `torch.load(weights_only=True)` exposing uninitialized pybind11-backed objects (such as DTensor placements) when a checkpoint uses the `NEWOBJ` opcode without a matching `BUILD`; such checkpoints are now rejected as corrupt or malicious (#194647) - Fix a stack buffer overflow in `torch_shm_manager` (libshm) when the Unix socket path is too long (e.g. a long `TMPDIR`); it now raises an error (#195183) - After `import torch.distributed`, `torch.load(weights_only=True)` and `get_unsafe_globals_in_checkpoint` no longer treat builtin exceptions as safe globals (a process-wide allowlist added in 2.14), and loading no longer calls overridden `append`/`extend` on allowlisted `list` subclasses. Checkpoints with pickled exceptions now need `torch.serialization.add_safe_globals`; object collectives are unchanged (#200956) # Developers ## Distributed (c10d) - Make `FakeProcessGroup` support `all_to_all_single` with any sizes and add a `simulate_uniform_ranks` option (#193985, #194545) - Fix a clang build error and add `amd_smi` as a ROCm 7.14+ build dependency (#194104, #192520) - Add the private `torch.distributed._functional_collectives.wait_tensors`, which waits on all outputs of a multi-output functional collective at once; `torch.compile` uses it for coalesced collectives and `batch_isend_irecv` (#193892) ## Profiler - Kineto source now lives in `third_party/kineto` instead of a git submodule (#198648) - Remove the ignored `profiler_metrics` and `profiler_measure_per_kernel` `_ExperimentalConfig` arguments (now a `TypeError`), and deprecate the no-op `adjust_profiler_step` option (#198262, #193042) ## FX - Fix type annotations on `Tracer(autowrap_modules=...)` and `CodeGen.process_inputs` (#195467, #188287) ## Inductor - Add `DeviceInterface` and `DeviceOpOverrides` extension points for out-of-tree accelerator backends (#190326, #190614, #192896, #193908, #190615) - Add declarative `implies` support to Inductor/Dynamo `Config` (#196663) ## Ahead-Of-Time Inductor (AOTI) - Add `DeviceOpOverrides.aten_device_type()` so backends provide their ATen device type to AOTInductor C++ codegen (#193904) ## C++ Frontend - `c10::List` iterators satisfy `std::random_access_iterator`, and `List ::emplace` now constructs a `T` (#196002) ## Developer Experience - Add `spin test` to run `pytest` or `test/run_test.py` like CI (#198649) ## Build Frontend - Add an opt-in `USE_CMAKE_INSTRUMENTATION=1` build option to collect build metrics (CMake >= 4.3) (#189455) - Turn off `USE_FLASH_ATTENTION` automatically when no target CUDA architecture is sm80 or newer (#194502) - Fix the misspelled `CUDA_LIMIT_GPU_ARCHITECTURE` in CUDA architecture autodetection (#195695) - Honor `USE_MIMALLOC=OFF` on Windows and AArch64 (#199064) - Fix the FlashAttention CUDA build on Windows with MSVC in C++20 mode (#197382) ## Release Engineering - Move the CD wheel build scripts under `.ci/wheel/` (`.ci/manywheel/` to `.ci/wheel/linux/`, `.ci/macwheel/` to `.ci/wheel/mac/`, and the Windows pipeline to `.ci/wheel/windows/`) and share one `numpy` build pin (#189275) - Add a native-AOT stage to CUDA builds that exports CuTeDSL and Triton kernels ahead of time and embeds them into `libtorch_cuda`. The stage skips itself when it does not apply (for example CUDA older than 13 or no supported GPU architecture), but once it decides to export, a missing `nvidia-cutlass-dsl` (or Triton, installable with `scripts/install_triton_wheel.sh`) is a hard error; set `TORCH_NATIVE_AOT=0` to skip the stage (#194243, #196747, #196507) - Fix the CMake C and C++ compiler flag checks sharing one cache variable, so a result for one language could be reused for the other; the generated `HAS_ ` variables are now prefixed `HAS_C` and `HAS_CXX` (#197614) - Add a persistent `[no-ci]` PR title prefix that skips build, test and lint jobs, and make `@pytorchbot merge -i` ignore current failures across every PR in a ghstack stack (#196534, #197143) ## CUDA - Update the bundled CUTLASS to v4.8.0 and CUTLASS-Operators to v0.3.0 (#198179) ## CPU (AArch64) - Add the `AT_VEC_CUSTOM_MATH` compile definition, which hides the built-in vectorized math functions on AVX2, AVX512, NEON and SVE256 builds so that a vectorized math library other than SLEEF can be plugged in (#197419) ## MPS - Fix building with clang 16 and Apple clang 15 (#199115) - Fix building with a Metal 4 toolchain against older macOS SDKs, and deprecation warnings with the macOS 27 SDK (#196104, #197200) - `at::mps::MPSProfiler` `begin*`/`end*` methods take the `MPSStream*`; stream-less `begin*` overloads are deprecated (#192525, #193611) - Fix macOS builds failing on SDKs that lack the Metal 4 cooperative-tensor APIs (#195302) - Fix stale embedded Metal shaders in incremental macOS builds (#196202) - Fix MPS shader includes in editable installs (#195295) ## ROCm - `torch.utils.cpp_extension.ROCM_VERSION` now uses the ROCm SDK version instead of the HIP runtime version, and `collect_env` reports both (#194985, #193602) ## XPU - Build XPU with pure SYCL compilation and support Clang as the host compiler; expose `USE_SYCLTLA` and enable oneMKL sparse in the build system (#194185, #198720, #196387, #198200) - Upgrade oneDNN to v3.13 (#196712) ## Caffe2 - Fix source builds with CUDA 13.3 (#194659)

Use `1.4.0rc2.post1` when installing the Python package. The wheel-only patch removes a direct Git dependency that prevented PyPI publication (#21128) and updates the Boost download mirror used during builds (#21133). items.title: v0.8.0
items.abstract_or_text: ## Overview This release adds the LiquidAI LFM3 family (text, vision, audio and omni) together with a new experimental streaming-audio API in `mtmd`, and wires realtime audio in and out of the server through the new `/v1/realtime` and `/tts` endpoints. A batch of new architectures landed: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, SenseNova U1, Beam, Kolibri-1, Flint, Muse Spark, Granite Switch Decision, plus decision/embedding models from LiquidAI, Baidu and NVIDIA. The core got sparse-attention (QSA/DSA) reworked onto a fused masking op, a 50/50 SLRU cache for host-resident MoE experts, and cleaner `no_alloc` memory handling; the server got router memory-management and tool-calling improvements; the UI can now browse and download models straight from HF Hub, search conversations and compact them. Finally, `ggml` was bumped to v0.28.0, bringing `GGML_OP_TOP_K_MASK`, `-1` expert-index semantics and large backend performance work (CUDA chunked graph launches, SYCL graph replay, OpenCL Q2_K/Q3_K, Hexagon HTP rework, KleidiAI SVE kernels). ### Highlights - LFM3 family: LFM3-1.7B (text) and LFM3-VL-2B (vision), verified against the reference HF implementation [llama/31252](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31252) - LFM3-Audio-2B and LFM3-Omni-2B: ASR, TTS and voice chat from a single model, with streaming audio input and output [llama/31257](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31257) ### API changes - DRY sampler: new `LLAMA_DRY_MAX_SEQ_BREAKERS` (64) caps distinct sequence breakers, each costing `O(n_vocab)` at init [llama/31035](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31035) - `mtmd`: new experimental `mtmd_audio_stream` API turning PCM fed as it arrives into decoder-ready embedding rows [llama/30629](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30629) - `mtmd`: audio generation is now stateful - `mtmd_gen_state` replaces the raw `state_data` buffers of the audio gen API [llama/30902](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30902) - `mtmd`: `mtmd_caps` gained `gen_audio`; new TTS types `SOPRANO` and `LFM3A`; repetition penalty for sampled codes [llama/28607](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28607) [llama/31257](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31257) - `mtmd_helper_get_capabilities()` to query the capabilities of an mmproj file from helper code [llama/31183](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31183) - Server: new `/v1/realtime` endpoint implementing the OpenAI realtime protocol for conversation and transcription [llama/31269](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31269) [llama/30636](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30636) - Server: new `POST /tts` endpoint for text-to-speech items.abstract_or_text: hexagon: add conv2d support (#30995) * hexagon: add conv2d op * hex-conv2d: add double-buffered staging * hex-conv2d: full 64-wide activation block transpose straight from staged buffer * hex-conv2d: implicit gemm * hex-conv2d: remove scalar path and kernel * hex-conv2d: unify conv2d kernel params for all paths * hex-conv2d: scale HMX result before f16 storage and then restore during unpacking to prevent overflow * hex-conv2d: fix f16 overflow in HMX paths * hex-conv2d: refactor to rebase to new op fusion machinery * hex-conv2d: restructure DMA pipelines and trace scopes * hex-conv2d: removed the HVX_WIDTH and HVX_TILED paths * hex-conv2d: remove in-loop vector spills * hex-conv2d: refactor kparams, vtcm-layout and dma-pipeline to match the other ops * hex-conv2d: add basic support for CONV_2D_DW Co-Authored-By: Pranav Dhinakar * hex-conv_2d_dw: use DMA in all paths * hex-conv_2d_dw: support for chunking larger inputs * hex-conv_2d_dw: remove scalar/hvx access for w tensor (replaced with sync dma copy) * hex-conv-2d: fix warnings * hex-conv2d-dw: vectorize all paths * hex-conv-2d-dw: tree-based reductions and unrolling to optimize * hex-conv-2d-dw: uninline compute loops from dma loops * hex-conv-2d-dw: move all kernel selection into the host solver and simplify/specialize kernel dispatch * hex-softmax: update obsolete gates to enable SOFT_MAX for mmproj --------- Co-authored-by: Max Krasnyansky Co-authored-by: Pranav Dhinakar **Website:** - items.abstract_or_text: server: expose the reasoning effort levels of the chat template (#31271) * server: expose the reasoning effort levels of the chat template The capability probe renders a user turn for each candidate level (minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max) and for an unknown level. A level is honored when it renders without raising and differently from the unknown level, which shows the template fallback. Levels sharing a render are aliases and the highest one is kept. The caps serialize to JSON, and chat_template_caps in /props reports the list as reasoning_effort_levels, from lowest to highest. * jinja: keep the caps free of the json dependency The caps keep reporting their flags as a map, and the effort levels stay a plain member. common_chat_templates_get_caps() builds the JSON the server reports from both, so jinja depends on json only for the probe inputs. **Website:** - items.abstract_or_text: llama : build the k-pool sparse selection independently of the kq_mask shape (#31243) * llama : build the k-pool sparse selection independently of the kq_mask shape qwen4exp (QSA) and glm5-next pick cache cells by index and no longer read the kq_mask values, but they still shaped the selection like the dense kq_mask. Build the selection as [n_kv, n_tokens] over the cache cells instead, and split it into the streams of the K view right before the attention. This lets the dense mask change its layout (e.g. per-sequence row lists) without touching the sparse layers. * improve comment Co-authored-by: Georgi Gerganov * llama : drop the unused build_fused_top_k_mask args, review nits --------- Co-authored-by: Georgi Gerganov **Website:** - items.abstract_or_text: tests : speed up tensor data generation and model saving (#31145) * tests : speed up tensor data generation and model saving Refactor save_models to create only the model, not a llama_context, which is not needed for saving. Replace the slow std::normal_distribution draw with a splitmix64 + box-muller normal generator. Assisted-by: dsh:llama.cpp/ggml-org/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp-GGUF (Mac Studio, M2 Ultra, 192GB) * tests : use a shared pool of normal draws for tensor data Generate a pool of normal draws once with std::mt19937 and std::normal_distribution, then have every tensor copy a cyclic slice of it instead of running a per-tensor box-muller. The name-keyed slice selection keeps the draw deterministic. Assisted-by: dsh:llama.cpp/ggml-org/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp-GGUF (Mac Studio, M2 Ultra, 192GB) * tests : log the size of saved models Report the produced file size in bytes and MB after each save. items.abstract_or_text: vulkan: fix CI llvmpipe by allowing dim 3 broadcast in MUL_MAT (#31239) * vulkan: allow dim 3 broadcast in MUL_MAT supports_op rejected every MUL_MAT whose src0 and src1 differ in ne3, although mul_mm, mul_mmq and mul_mat_vec already broadcast src0 over dim 3 through broadcast3. Such a matmul then ran on the CPU with a copy of the weight, and the split layout changed with the number of streams in the ubatch. Keep the strict check for MUL_MAT_ID only, and route the broadcast cases away from mul_mat_vec_nc, the one path that requires equal ne3. * tests : harden MUL_MAT with permuted dim 3 broadcast cases Harden the MUL_MAT coverage with a weight broadcast over dim 3 against a permuted per-stream activation, the shape of an MLA output projection with a non unified KV cache, for a single token, several heads and several tokens per stream. **Website:** - items.abstract_or_text: server: add router device memory margin parameter for dynamic unloading (#21231) * server: add --models-memory-max parameter to allow dynamically unloading models when they exceed a memory size threshold estimate with to-be-loaded model size included use no_alloc to get memory requirements for model load only set model memory_mb if not previously calculated use memory margin instead of total size limit, apply to each device separately add server memory debug logging move llama_context_device_memory function to llama-ext.h fix model count exceeded check improve memory_per_device map naming improve variable naming, fix style also strip models memory margin from child processes cont : clean-up replace device memory map with buft memory map. Use llama_get_memory_breakdown extract duplicated check into helper function move model memory estimation to subprocess precompute name->buft map, map GPU host types to CPU buft cleanup unused variable remove duplicated init calls * adapt to upstream changes * wip * common_memory_reports internface * SERVER_ROLE_MEASURE * server-models-sched * fix build * server : fix memory accounting of measure children and claim spin A measure child runs no_alloc, so the free memory it reports does not include its estimate: subtracting self there erased the memory held by other processes, down to zero with --fit on, and the next load could overshoot the margin. Subtract self only for instance reports. A queued load only checked --models-max before claiming, so when the memory margin blocked it behind a busy model, load() threw and the waiter retried in a tight loop. Refuse the claim while the limits are exceeded and no idle model can be unloaded, so the waiter sleeps on the condition variable until one goes idle. --------- Co-authored-by: Xuan Son Nguyen Co-authored-by: Pascal **Website:** - items.abstract_or_text: model: Add MiniCPM-OCR-Jev (#30980) * model : add MiniCPM-OCR-Jev support The model is a Qwen3.5-VL trunk with a value head read at the last token: it scores an OCR text against an image rendered from it, it does not generate. Add the openbmb-minicpm-ocr-jev decision type, served by POST /v1/systemone. The class scores are the pooled output of the sequence, read with last pooling, so the conversion turns score.weight into cls.output and sets embedding_length_out. The checkpoint has no LM head, so text generation is rejected instead of using the output weights duplicated from the token embeddings. The task is fixed, so its prompt is entirely in the systemone template, the same way h2o-lightning keeps its default there. The processor of the checkpoint allows up to 16384 merged tokens per image, more than the Qwen-VL default of mtmd, so the mmproj keeps the image budget of the preprocessor config. The checkpoint declares MiniCPMOCRForSequenceClassification in its config.json, as other models do. items.abstract_or_text: ggml : relax scale to non-contiguous views (#31146) * ggml : relax scale to non-contiguous views SCALE requires src0 to be 1D-contiguous. Relax this to dim-0 contiguity with arbitrary row strides (ggml_is_contiguous_rows), same as the unary ops in the Metal backend. - ggml: relax the assert in ggml_scale_impl - cpu: address src0 rows through their byte strides (f32, bf16) - cuda: stride-aware kernel, fastdiv row decomposition - metal: support bf16 scale (guarded unary instantiations) - sycl: keep the gate at contiguous, the kernel is flat f32 Add view variants to test_scale. Verified on CPU, Metal and CUDA. Assisted-by: dsh:llama.cpp/ggml-org/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF (RTX 5090 32GB, DDR5 128GB) * cuda : skip the softcap fusion on non-contiguous views The fused softcap kernel reads src and writes dst as dense arrays, so a view reaching SCALE -> TANH -> SCALE now that SCALE accepts non-contiguous rows would be read wrongly. Keep such graphs on the strided kernels until the fusion becomes stride aware. --------- Co-authored-by: Pascal **Website:** - **Attestations:** - **macOS/iOS:** - [macOS Apple Silicon (arm64)](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases/download/b11923/llama-b11923-bin-macos-arm64.tar.gz) - items.abstract_or_text: tests : fix multi-seq split replay and partial-state cases for trained models (#31216) * tests : fix multi-seq split replay against trained models The rollback snapshot is captured by the graph that decoded the rolled-back tail, while the reference context decodes the same prefix with different batch shapes. The two states differ in the last bits and trained models amplify the difference with every replayed token. Compare only the first replayed token of each seq, then restore the rollback state into the reference context before the seq-1-only tail. Assisted-by: dsh:llama.cpp/ggml-org/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF (MacBook, M5 Max, 128GB) * tests : require bit-exact seq-1 isolation in split replay The seq state save is not always bit-lossless - SWA-masked cells are not saved - so reload the restored state back into the rollback context. That way both contexts enter the seq-1-only tail with byte-identical memory, including the cell layout, and the tail logits must match bit-exact. Also assert that the restored state round-trips bit-identical. Assisted-by: dsh:llama.cpp/ggml-org/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF (MacBook, M5 Max, 128GB) * tests : drop the n_swa partial-state check from ps The check keys off llama_model_n_swa(), which returns 0 for dsv4 even though its raw KV cache has a 128-cell sliding window. The partial state grows with the tokens there by design, so the flatness check is wrong. Keep the partial **Website:** - **Attestations:** - **macOS/iOS:** - [macOS Apple Silicon (arm64)](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases/download/b11922/llama-b11922-bin-macos-arm64.tar.gz) - items.abstract_or_text: ## What's Changed * [CuTe, Fwd, SM100] Prevent NaN contamination from unused V cache entries by @fusheng-ji in https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/pull/2983 * [CuTe] Format config.py with ruff so the Lint workflow passes again by @WeiYedi in https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/pull/3067 * [CuTe, Bwd, SM100] Bound the K/V TMA loads by seqlen_k so unused rows cannot poison dQ (packed varlen and dense seqused_k) by @yunweili3 in https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/pull/3012 * [CuTe, SM90] Bound the K/V TMA loads by seqlen_k (fwd + bwd, packed varlen and dense seqused_k) by @yunweili3 in https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/pull/3013 * [CuTe] Bound ragged K/V TMA loads with per-CTA descriptor updates instead of a wrap-around descriptor by @yunweili3 in https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/pull/3071 * [CuTe, SM100] Unify hd256 backward (4/7): pack the query heads of a KV head into the Q tile (GQA) by @Johnsonms in https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/pull/2967 * [CuTe, SM100] Fix 2CTA CLC tile coords and make forward work-tile coordinates logical by @drisspg in https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/pull/3034 ## New Contributors * @fusheng-ji made their first contribution in https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/pull/2983 * @WeiYedi made their first contribution in https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/pull/3067 **Full Changelog**: https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/compare/fa4-v4.0.0.beta36...fa4-v4.0.0.beta37
